newsitem.title: GERMANY: Uptrend seen intact for bullish German shares.
newsitem.headline: Uptrend seen intact for bullish German shares.

text.p: German shares held their gains in post-bourse dealings on Thursday, hovering near all-time highs hit earlier in the day and with dealers' eyes still fixed on the crucial 3,000 point level on the DAX.
"It might be time for a bit of consolidation. But there is still an upside in this market," said one Munich dealer.
"The champagne bottles will be out," said a Frankfurt trader. "The uptrend is definitely still there."
The IBIS DAX index was up 18.84 points at 2,995.40 points at 1442 GMT, supported by gains in early Wall Street and the buoyant DAX futures market.

Dealers said the German share market was in an ideal position, amid hopes for strong corporate earnings this year, especially after the dollar's recent advance, signs of moderate inflation and little risk of an interest rate rise.

However some cautioned that the cash market was at present very vulnerable to shifts on the futures market, which has been volatile ahead of expiry of some DAX futures contracts tomorrow and will continue to be in the short term.
DTB March DAX futures were up 17 points at 3,007 points.
Gains on the March future earlier sparked the DAX's ascent to an all-time intraday high of 2,998.61.
But other dealers said there was more than enough cash in the market to support a continued rally, particularly from international funds.
Banks were the clear favourites of the day, benefiting from a move out of the chemicals sector in favour of financials.
Deutsche Bank AG held its gains in afternoon dealings to trade up 1.78 marks at 78.40 while other bank shares were also well ahead.
Meanwhile chemicals, notably BASF AG and Hoechst AG were down 76 pfennigs at 59.54 and down 51 pfennigs at 69.65 marks respectively.
Utility RWE AG remained ahead, up 99 pfennigs at 68.85 marks, after news that it was to receive partial damages for delays in operating a nuclear power plant.
Steelmaker Thyssen AG was down 4.75 marks at 283.50 marks after its Thyssen Stahl unit reported a sharp drop in 1995/1996 profits.
"That just shows what can still happen to this market if the corporate news is bad," one dealer remarked.
